advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a non-LockTimeout exception (e.g. a CommandError not starting with 'flock:') is NOT retried: emit returns False after exactly one append_event attempt.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:81-83: 'except Exception as exc:  / if not _is_lock_timeout_error(exc): / raise'
src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:63: 'return getattr(exc, "returncode", None) == 1 and str(exc).startswith("flock:")' — the discriminator this diff adds

The only permanent-failure test (test_pass_sidecar_permanent_lock_timeout_returns_false) raises LockTimeout on every call, exercising ONLY the retryable branch; ABSENCE of any test injecting a non-lock error to prove it is not retried and returns False on the first attempt.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the non-LockTimeout branch of the new retry-discrimination logic: _append_sidecar_retrying re-raises immediately when _is_lock_timeout_error(exc) is False, but no test asserts that a non-lock exception (e.g. a plain StoreError / a CommandError whose message does NOT start with 'flock:') is NOT retried and causes emit to return False after exactly one attempt. A regression that made _is_lock_timeout_error over-match or that retried all exceptions would pass every existing test.
scenarios: A permanent (non-transient) store write error is silently retried, adding latency, if _is_lock_timeout_error is later broadened
A future change to the discriminator that stops recognizing the wrapped-vs-raw distinction goes uncaught
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches _seam.append_event to raise a non-lock error (e.g. CommandError('boom')) counting calls, then assert calls['n'] == 1 and completion_sidecar.emit(...) is False.
